claim: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infects an estimated 71 million people worldwide.
source: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infects an estimated 71 million people worldwide (World Health Organization, 2017)
evidence: Supported by citation to World Health Organization, 2017

claim: HCV has been classified into seven distinct genotypes.
source: The virus is highly variable and has been classified into seven distinct genotypes, and further divided into 67 subtypes, based on nucleotide sequence diversity (Simmonds, 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Simmonds, 2004

claim: HCV has been divided into 67 subtypes based on nucleotide sequence diversity.
source: The virus is highly variable and has been classified into seven distinct genotypes, and further divided into 67 subtypes, based on nucleotide sequence diversity (Simmonds, 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Simmonds, 2004

claim: An intronic SNP rs12979860 in the IFNL4 gene is associated with 11 amino acid polymorphisms on the HCV polyprotein at a 5% false discovery rate.
source: Using a systematic genome-to-genome approach in a cohort of chronically infected patients, we recently reported associations between an intronic single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs12979860 in the interferon lambda 4 (IFNL4) gene (CC vs. non-CC) and 11 amino acid polymorphisms on the HCV polyprotein (Ansari et al., 2017) at a 5% false discovery rate (FDR) (Benjamini and Hochberg, 1995).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ansari et al., 2017 and Benjamini and Hochberg, 1995

claim: IFNL4 is a member of the type III interferon (IFN-λ) family that act as cytokines as part of the innate immune system and lack apparent epitope specificity.
source: This observation was unexpected since IFNL4 is a member of the type III interferon (IFN-λ) family that act as cytokines as part of the innate immune system and therefore lack apparent epitope specificity (Bruening et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bruening et al., 2017

claim: Variants within the IFNL4 locus contribute to spontaneous virus clearance in HCV infection.
source: These associations between polymorphisms on the HCV polyprotein and host IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 genotypes are further intriguing given that variants within the IFNL4 locus (including SNP rs12979860) contribute to HCV clinical and biological outcomes, including spontaneous virus clearance, response to IFN-based treatment, viral load and liver disease progression (Aoki et al., 2015; Ge et al., 2009; Noureddin et al., 2013; Patin et al., 2012; Rauch et al., 2010; Suppiah et al., 2009; Tanaka et al., 2009; Thomas et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Variants within the IFNL4 locus contribute to response to IFN-based treatment in HCV infection.

evidence: Supported by multiple citations

source: The intronic IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 is in high linkage disequilibrium with other SNPs that may be more biologically relevant, including the exonic dinucleotide variant rs368234815 (r2 = 0.975 CEU population, 1000 Genomes dataset) in IFNL4.
evidence: Supported by reference to 1000 Genomes dataset

claim: The variant rs368234815 [ΔG > TT] causes a frameshift, abrogating production of functional IFN-λ4 protein.
source: This variant [ΔG > TT] causes a frameshift, abrogating production of functional IFN-λ4 protein (Prokunina-Olsson et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Prokunina-Olsson et al., 2013

claim: Several amino acid substitutions within IFN-λ4 alter its antiviral activity.
source: Moreover, several amino acid substitutions within IFN-λ4 have been shown to alter its antiviral activity (Bamford et al., 2018; Terczyńska-Dyla et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bamford et al., 2018 and Terczyńska-Dyla et al., 2014

claim: A common amino acid substitution coded by SNP rs117648444 [G > A] in the IFN-λ4 protein changes a proline residue at position 70 (P70) to a serine residue (S70).
source: In particular, a common amino acid substitution (coded by the SNP rs117648444 [G > A]) in the IFN-λ4 protein, which changes a proline residue at position 70 (P70) to a serine residue (S70), reduces its antiviral activity in vitro (Terczyńska-Dyla et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Terczyńska-Dyla et al., 2014

claim: The P70S substitution in IFN-λ4 reduces its antiviral activity in vitro.
source: In particular, a common amino acid substitution (coded by the SNP rs117648444 [G > A]) in the IFN-λ4 protein, which changes a proline residue at position 70 (P70) to a serine residue (S70), reduces its antiviral activity in vitro (Terczyńska-Dyla et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Terczyńska-Dyla et al., 2014

claim: The combination of alleles at rs368234815 and rs117648444 creates four potential haplotypes: TT/G, TT/A, ΔG/G, and ΔG/A.
source: Thus, the combination of alleles at rs368234815 and rs117648444 creates four potential haplotypes, two that do not produce IFN-λ4 protein (TT/G or TT/A; IFN-λ4-Null) and two that result in production of two IFN-λ4 protein variants (ΔG/G; IFN-λ4-P70 and ΔG/A; IFN-λ4-S70).
evidence: Based on logical inference from the genetic variants described

claim: Patients harbouring the impaired IFN-λ4-S70 variant display lower hepatic interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) expression levels compared to patients carrying the IFN-λ4-P70 variant.
source: Patients harbouring the impaired IFN-λ4-S70 variant display lower hepatic interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) expression levels, which is associated with increased viral clearance following acute infection and a better response to IFN-based therapy, compared to patients carrying the more active IFN-λ4-P70 variant (Eslam et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Eslam et al., 2017

claim: Lower hepatic ISG expression is associated with increased viral clearance following acute HCV infection.
source: Patients harbouring the impaired IFN-λ4-S70 variant display lower hepatic interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) expression levels, which is associated with increased viral clearance following acute infection and a better response to IFN-based therapy, compared to patients carrying the more active IFN-λ4-P70 variant (Eslam et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Eslam et al., 2017

claim: Lower hepatic ISG expression is associated with a better response to IFN-based therapy in HCV infection.
source: Patients harbouring the impaired IFN-λ4-S70 variant display lower hepatic interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) expression levels, which is associated with increased viral clearance following acute infection and a better response to IFN-based therapy, compared to patients carrying the more active IFN-λ4-P70 variant (Eslam et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Eslam et al., 2017

claim: 42 viral sites on the HCV polyprotein are significantly associated with IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 at a 5% FDR.
source: At a 5% FDR, 42 of the viral sites tested were associated with IFNL4 SNP rs12979860, increasing to 76 sites at a 10% FDR (Figure 1 and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by data analysis and shown in Figure 1

claim: 76 viral sites on the HCV polyprotein are significantly associated with IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 at a 10% FDR.
source: At a 5% FDR, 42 of the viral sites tested were associated with IFNL4 SNP rs12979860, increasing to 76 sites at a 10% FDR (Figure 1 and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by data analysis and shown in Figure 1

claim: The IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 affects 1.4% of all viral amino acids in the HCV genotype 3a polyprotein at a 5% FDR.
source: This represented 1.4% at a 5% FDR and 2.5% at a 10% FDR of all the viral amino acids in the HCV genotype 3a polyprotein (N = 3021), reflecting a large impact of the host IFNL4 locus on the amino acids encoded at variable sites on the viral polyprotein.
evidence: Calculated from the data analysis results

claim: The IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 affects 2.5% of all viral amino acids in the HCV genotype 3a polyprotein at a 10% FDR.
source: This represented 1.4% at a 5% FDR and 2.5% at a 10% FDR of all the viral amino acids in the HCV genotype 3a polyprotein (N = 3021), reflecting a large impact of the host IFNL4 locus on the amino acids encoded at variable sites on the viral polyprotein.
evidence: Calculated from the data analysis results

claim: The most associated viral site with IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 is at position 2570 in the NS5B protein (p=1.32×10−8, log(OR)=1.19).
source: The most associated viral site was at position 2570 in the NS5B protein (p=1.32×10−8, log(OR)=1.19), as previously reported (Ansari et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by data analysis and citation to Ansari et al., 2017

claim: 26 of the 76 sites (34%) associated with the IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 at a 10% FDR lie within the HCV E2 glycoprotein.
source: Notably, 26 of the 76 sites (34%) associated with the IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 at a 10% FDR lie within the HCV E2 glycoprotein (Appendix 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Supported by data analysis and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5

claim: No significantly enhanced enrichment or depletion for association signals was observed in any specific viral protein.
source: However, we did not observe significantly enhanced enrichment or depletion for association signals in any specific viral protein, or in previously reported HLA restricted epitope regions in HCV genotype 3a (von Delft et al., 2016) (Supplementary file 3 and Materials and methods).
evidence: Supported by data analysis and citation to von Delft et al., 2016

claim: No significantly enhanced enrichment or depletion for association signals was observed in previously reported HLA restricted epitope regions in HCV genotype 3a.
source: However, we did not observe significantly enhanced enrichment or depletion for association signals in any specific viral protein, or in previously reported HLA restricted epitope regions in HCV genotype 3a (von Delft et al., 2016) (Supplementary file 3 and Materials and methods).
evidence: Supported by data analysis and citation to von Delft et al., 2016

claim: The study included 485 patients of white ancestry infected with HCV genotype 3a from two cohorts (BOSON N=411, EAP N=74).
source: To ensure that host and virus population structures had a minimal impact on our results, we used paired genome-wide human and viral genetic data in a homogenous group of 485 patients with self reported white ancestry, infected with HCV genotype 3a from two cohorts [BOSON (Foster et al., 2015) and Expanded Access Program (EAP) (Foster et al., 2016) cohorts, NBOSON = 411, NEAP = 74, see Supplementary file 1 and Materials and methods for a description of the cohorts].
evidence: Description of study cohort with citations to Foster et al., 2015 and Foster et al., 2016

claim: The first and second viral principal components explained around 3% and 2% of variance in HCV nucleotide diversity respectively.
source: The first and second viral principal components (PCs) explained around 3% and 2% of variance in HCV nucleotide diversity respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b), indicating a homogenous group of isolates as observed by the long terminal and short internal branches of the phylogenetic tree (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: Supported by PCA analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b

claim: Host IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 genotypes were randomly distributed on the viral phylogenetic tree (treeBreaker Bayes factor = 1.1).
source: This observation was not reflected in host IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 genotypes, which were randomly distributed on the viral phylogenetic tree (treeBreaker Bayes factor = 1.1, Figure 1—figure supplement 3b).
evidence: Supported by treeBreaker analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3b

claim: Associations were observed between the host IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 and the fifth viral PC (p=1.3×10−15).
source: However, we did observe associations between the host IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 and the fifth and seventh viral PCs (p=1.3×10−15 and 7.2 × 10−9, respectively), which were not directed by host-virus population co-structuring, suggesting that the IFNL4 locus drives HCV nucleotide diversity (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b–d and Appendix 1).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: Associations were observed between the host IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 and the seventh viral PC (p=7.2×10−9).

evidence: Supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: The IFNL4 locus drives HCV nucleotide diversity.
source: However, we did observe associations between the host IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 and the fifth and seventh viral PCs (p=1.3×10−15 and 7.2 × 10−9, respectively), which were not directed by host-virus population co-structuring, suggesting that the IFNL4 locus drives HCV nucleotide diversity (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b–d and Appendix 1).
evidence: Inferred from the association between IFNL4 SNP and viral PCs

claim: 977 tests were performed at 471 viral sites for association between IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 genotypes and virus-encoded amino acids.
source: Presence or absence of each viral amino acid was used as the response variable; 977 tests were performed at 471 viral sites.
evidence: Description of the statistical analysis performed

claim: Cirrhosis status, cohorts, gender, and age were not associated with any specific amino acids at a 10% FDR.
source: To test for possible confounders we separately added each of the cirrhosis status of patients, cohorts (BOSON vs. EAP), gender and age to the model as covariates. These covariates were not associated with any specific amino acids at a 10% FDR (data not shown).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis

claim: Non-synonymous changes at 16 viral codons were significantly associated with IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 at a 5% FDR.
source: We observed that non-synonymous changes at 16 viral codons were significantly associated with IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 at a 5% FDR, increasing to 35 viral codons at a 10% FDR (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: Supported by codon-level analysis

claim: Non-synonymous changes at 35 viral codons were significantly associated with IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 at a 10% FDR.
source: We observed that non-synonymous changes at 16 viral codons were significantly associated with IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 at a 5% FDR, increasing to 35 viral codons at a 10% FDR (Supplementary file 5).

claim: Synonymous changes at two viral codons were significantly associated with IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 at a 5% FDR.

claim: Synonymous changes at four viral codons were significantly associated with IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 at a 10% FDR.

claim: The effect of the IFNL4 locus on virus sequence diversity is mostly at the amino acid level.
source: This indicates that the effect of the IFNL4 locus on virus sequence diversity is mostly at the amino acid level, although a small impact on nucleotide substitutions cannot be excluded.
evidence: Inferred from the comparison of synonymous and non-synonymous associations

claim: Most viruses suppress genomic CpG and UpA dinucleotide frequencies to mimic host mRNA composition and avoid the immune response.
source: Most viruses suppress genomic CpG and UpA dinucleotide frequencies, supposedly to mimic host mRNA composition and avoid the immune response (Simmonds et al., 2013).

claim: Genetic variants in the human IFNL4 locus drive widespread sequence changes across the entire HCV polyprotein.
source: Here, we show that genetic variants in the human IFNL4 locus drive widespread sequence changes across the entire HCV polyprotein - much larger than we previously reported (Ansari et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by the genome-wide association study results and citation to Ansari et al., 2017

claim: The IFNL4 locus affects the HCV genome at the nucleotide sequence level.
source: We also report an association of the IFNL4 locus with synonymous codon variants, suggesting that this locus might also affect the HCV genome at the nucleotide sequence level.
evidence: Inferred from the association with synonymous codon variants

claim: The IFNL4 haplotype coding for the IFN-λ4-S70 variant has a smaller impact on viral load compared to the haplotype coding for the IFN-λ4-P70 variant.
source: Finally, we report that the IFNL4 haplotype coding for the IFN-λ4-S70 variant has a smaller impact on viral load and viral amino acid variation at associated sites compared to the haplotype coding for the more active IFN-λ4-P70 variant.
evidence: Supported by the viral load and effect size analyses

claim: The IFNL4 haplotype coding for the IFN-λ4-S70 variant has a smaller impact on viral amino acid variation at associated sites compared to the haplotype coding for the IFN-λ4-P70 variant.
source: Finally, we report that the IFNL4 haplotype coding for the IFN-λ4-S70 variant has a smaller impact on viral load and viral amino acid variation at associated sites compared to the haplotype coding for the more active IFN-λ4-P70 variant.
evidence: Supported by the effect size analyses

claim: The IFNL4 gene mediates HCV amino acid variation.
source: This indicates that the IFNL4 gene not only mediates HCV amino acid variation but also modulates viral load in patients.
evidence: Concluded from the association and effect size analyses

claim: The IFNL4 gene modulates viral load in HCV-infected patients.
source: This indicates that the IFNL4 gene not only mediates HCV amino acid variation but also modulates viral load in patients.
evidence: Supported by the viral load analyses

claim: 2.5% of HCV-encoded amino acids across the polyprotein were significantly associated with host IFNL4 SNP at a 10% FDR.
source: We selected patients chronically infected with HCV genotype 3a and of self-reported white ancestry to limit the impact of human and viral population co-structuring in our analyses. We observed that 2.5% of HCV-encoded amino acids across the polyprotein were significantly associated with host IFNL4 SNP at a 10% FDR.
evidence: Supported by the genome-wide association study results

claim: 0.7% of the HCV amino acids were associated with HLA class I and II alleles at a 5% FDR.
source: In comparison, we previously reported that 0.7% of the HCV amino acids were associated with HLA class I and II alleles (Ansari et al., 2017) at a 5% FDR.
evidence: Supported by citation to Ansari et al., 2017

claim: The impact of the innate immune response on HCV amino acid variation is comparable to that of the T cell response.
source: Thus, although both arms of the adaptive immune system direct amino acid selection through pressure on epitopes recognised by T and B cell responses to infection, our results show that the innate immune response also has the capacity to drive particular polymorphisms in HCV-encoded proteins and that its impact is comparable to that of the T cell response (as indicated by HCV amino acid variants associated with HLA alleles).
evidence: Inferred from comparison of association percentages between IFNL4 and HLA

claim: IFN-λ4 may exert its impact through a previously unknown mechanism or at more than one stage of the virus life cycle.
source: Given that we did not observe any significant enhancement or depletion of association signals in a specific viral protein or in HLA-restricted epitopes, IFN-λ4 may exert its impact through a previously unknown mechanism or at more than one stage of the virus life cycle.
evidence: Speculative inference based on the lack of enrichment in specific proteins or epitopes

claim: IFN-λ4 induces a large number of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs), many of which are largely unstudied or poorly characterised.
source: In common with other IFNs, IFN-λ4 induces a large number of ISGs, many of which are largely unstudied or poorly characterised.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about interferons

claim: Ribonuclease L (RNase-L) is an ISG that cleaves viral RNA to control viral infections in animals.
source: The HCV UpA dinucleotide frequency was significantly associated with the IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 genotypes; interestingly, ribonuclease L (RNase-L), an ISG that cleaves viral RNA to control viral infections in animals (Ding and Voinnet, 2007), targets both UpA and UpU dinucleotides (Wreschner et al., 1981).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ding and Voinnet, 2007 and Wreschner et al., 1981

claim: RNase-L targets both UpA and UpU dinucleotides.
source: The HCV UpA dinucleotide frequency was significantly associated with the IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 genotypes; interestingly, ribonuclease L (RNase-L), an ISG that cleaves viral RNA to control viral infections in animals (Ding and Voinnet, 2007), targets both UpA and UpU dinucleotides (Wreschner et al., 1981).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wreschner et al., 1981

claim: HCV genotype 1 has a lower frequency of UpA and UpU dinucleotides than HCV genotypes 2 and 3.
source: Moreover, HCV genotype 1, which is relatively resistant to IFN-based therapy, has a lower frequency of UpA and UpU dinucleotides than the more IFN-sensitive HCV genotypes 2 and 3 (Dao Thi et al., 2012; Kong et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dao Thi et al., 2012 and Kong et al., 2012

claim: HCV genotype 1 is relatively resistant to IFN-based therapy.
source: Moreover, HCV genotype 1, which is relatively resistant to IFN-based therapy, has a lower frequency of UpA and UpU dinucleotides than the more IFN-sensitive HCV genotypes 2 and 3 (Dao Thi et al., 2012; Kong et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dao Thi et al., 2012 and Kong et al., 2012

claim: HCV genotypes 2 and 3 are more IFN-sensitive than genotype 1.
source: Moreover, HCV genotype 1, which is relatively resistant to IFN-based therapy, has a lower frequency of UpA and UpU dinucleotides than the more IFN-sensitive HCV genotypes 2 and 3 (Dao Thi et al., 2012; Kong et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dao Thi et al., 2012 and Kong et al., 2012

claim: The UpA dinucleotide is targeted by RNA-degrading enzymes and its presence in a RNA sequence accelerates its degradation in the cytoplasm.
source: Indeed, the UpA dinucleotide is targeted by RNA-degrading enzymes and its presence in a RNA sequence accelerates its degradation in the cytoplasm (Simmonds et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Simmonds et al., 2013

claim: The more stringent immune environment of non-CC patients may select virus with a lower UpA frequency.
source: It is possible that the more stringent immune environment of non-CC patients (with higher hepatic expression of ISGs) selects virus with a lower UpA frequency.
evidence: Speculative inference based on the association between IFNL4 genotype and UpA frequency

claim: IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 non-CC patients have a modest reduction (0.9%) in their viral UpA frequencies relative to CC patients.
source: However, we note that the IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 non-CC patients have a modest reduction (0.9%) in their viral UpA frequencies relative to the CC patients and that this reduction could be mediated by the widespread amino acid changes associated with the IFNL4 SNP rs12979860.
evidence: Calculated from the dinucleotide frequency analysis

claim: IFN-λ4-P70 and IFN-λ4-S70 variants of IFN-λ4 protein have distinct phenotypes, both in vivo and in vitro.
source: Previous studies have shown that IFN-λ4-P70 and IFN-λ4-S70 variants of IFN-λ4 protein have distinct phenotypes, both in vivo and in vitro.
evidence: Supported by references to previous studies

claim: The haplotype coding for the IFN-λ4-S70 variant had a smaller effect on viral amino acid variability compared to the haplotype coding for the IFN-λ4-P70 variant.
source: Using these data, we observed that the haplotype coding for the IFN-λ4-S70 variant had a smaller effect on viral amino acid variability compared to the haplotype coding for the IFN-λ4-P70 variant. This observation agrees with previous independent studies showing the reduced antiviral activity for IFN-λ4-S70 in vitro (Bamford et al., 2018; Terczyńska-Dyla et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by effect size analysis and citations to Bamford et al., 2018 and Terczyńska-Dyla et al., 2014

claim: Production of IFN-λ4 protein drives an altered immune response that mediates reduced viral load with a broad impact on viral amino acid diversity.
source: We conclude that production of IFN-λ4 protein drives an altered immune response that mediates reduced viral load with a broad impact on viral amino acid diversity.
evidence: Concluded from the combined analyses of viral load and amino acid associations

claim: Host IFNL4 gene can mediate selection of amino acids at specific sites on the HCV polyprotein.
source: In this study, we demonstrated by using paired host-HCV genomic data that host IFNL4 gene, a cytokine that is part of the innate immune response and not expected to target specific viral residues, can mediate selection of amino acids at specific sites on the HCV polyprotein.
evidence: Supported by the genome-wide association study results

claim: 1.4% of the HCV amino acids across the viral polyprotein are associated with host IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 at a 5% FDR.
source: We report that 1.4% (42/3021) of the HCV amino acids across the viral polyprotein are associated with host IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 at a 5% FDR and that the impact on amino acid variation is spread across all viral proteins.
evidence: Supported by the genome-wide association study results

claim: The impact of IFNL4 on amino acid variation is spread across all viral proteins.
source: We report that 1.4% (42/3021) of the HCV amino acids across the viral polyprotein are associated with host IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 at a 5% FDR and that the impact on amino acid variation is spread across all viral proteins.
evidence: Supported by the genome-wide association study results

claim: The impact of the innate immune response on HCV amino acid variation is comparable to that of the T cell response.
source: Thus, although both arms of the adaptive immune system direct amino acid selection through pressure on epitopes recognised by T and B cell responses to infection, our results show that the innate immune response also has the capacity to drive particular polymorphisms in HCV-encoded proteins and that its impact is comparable to that of the T cell response (as indicated by HCV amino acid variants associated with HLA alleles).
evidence: Inferred from comparison of association percentages

claim: The host B cell response largely restricts amino acid modifications to the envelope glycoproteins, in particular E2.
source: The only other major driver of HCV amino acid variation is the host B cell response, which is largely restricted to modifying amino acids in the envelope glycoproteins, in particular E2 (Ball et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ball et al., 2014

claim: The E2 glycoprotein contained the highest proportion of sites affected by IFNL4 SNP rs12979860.
source: Although there was no significant enrichment of associations comparing the structural with the non-structural proteins, the E2 glycoprotein contained the highest proportion of sites affected by IFNL4 SNP rs12979860.
evidence: Supported by the distribution of associated sites

claim: Many IFNL4-associated residues in E2 were located either in hypervariable region 1 (HVR1) or on the surface of the protein.
source: From mapping these sites onto previously known functional domains on E2, we found that many residues were located either in hypervariable region 1 (HVR1) or on the surface of the protein.
evidence: Inferred from mapping analysis

claim: Some IFNL4-associated sites in E2 coincided with epitopes that are targets for the antibody response or have a role in virus entry.
source: Indeed, some sites coincided with epitopes that are targets for the antibody response or have a role in virus entry (Appendix 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Inferred from mapping analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5

claim: The host response to HCV genotype 3a infection induces pathways including those affecting B cell development.
source: Since the host response to HCV genotype 3a infection induces pathways including those affecting B cell development (Robinson et al., 2015), we do not exclude the possibility that IFNL4 SNP rs12979860 genotype either influences B cell response to infection or the process of virus binding and entry.
evidence: Supported by citation to Robinson et al., 2015

claim: Variants in E2 emerge during establishment of chronic HCV infection that give enhanced resistance to interferon-induced transmembrane (IFITM) proteins.
source: Indeed, a recent report has demonstrated the emergence of variants in E2 during establishment of chronic infection that give enhanced resistance to interferon-induced transmembrane (IFITM) proteins (Wrensch et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wrensch et al., 2019

claim: One of the E2 residues that encoded a different amino acid as chronicity developed was at position 500, which is an IFNL4-associated site.
source: One of the E2 residues that encoded a different amino acid as chronicity developed was at position 500, which is an IFNL4-associated site (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by reference to Supplementary file 2

claim: IFITM proteins potently inhibit virus entry.
source: Given that IFITM proteins potently inhibit virus entry, it is possible that differences in IFITM induction between those who do and do not produce IFN-λ4 may account for some of the footprint observed in the E2 protein sequence.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about IFITM proteins

claim: IFITM proteins cooperate with anti-HCV neutralising antibodies to enhance restriction of virus entry.
source: Moreover, IFITM proteins cooperate with anti-HCV neutralising antibodies to enhance restriction of virus entry.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about IFITM proteins

claim: In HIV-infected patients, the rs368234815 variant has been associated with long-term non-progressor HIV-1 controllers.
source: In HIV-infected patients, the rs368234815 variant has been associated with long-term non-progressor HIV-1 controllers (Dominguez-Molina et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Dominguez-Molina et al., 2017

claim: In influenza virus infection, IFNL4 SNP rs8099917 was associated with increased sero-conversion after influenza vaccination.
source: In influenza virus infection, IFNL4 SNP rs8099917 was associated with increased sero-conversion after influenza vaccination (Egli et al., 2014a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Egli et al., 2014a

claim: IFNL4 variants have been associated with bronchiolitis.
source: IFNL4 variants have also been associated with bronchiolitis (Scagnolari et al., 2012), cytomegalovirus (Egli et al., 2014b) and Andes virus (Angulo et al., 2015) infections.
evidence: Supported by citation to Scagnolari et al., 2012

claim: IFNL4 variants have been associated with cytomegalovirus infection.
source: IFNL4 variants have also been associated with bronchiolitis (Scagnolari et al., 2012), cytomegalovirus (Egli et al., 2014b) and Andes virus (Angulo et al., 2015) infections.
evidence: Supported by citation to Egli et al., 2014b

claim: IFNL4 variants have been associated with Andes virus infection.
source: IFNL4 variants have also been associated with bronchiolitis (Scagnolari et al., 2012), cytomegalovirus (Egli et al., 2014b) and Andes virus (Angulo et al., 2015) infections.
evidence: Supported by citation to Angulo et al., 2015

claim: IFNL4 possibly plays a role in many viral infections and immune related diseases in the liver and other organs.
source: These observations suggest that IFNL4 possibly plays a role in many viral infections and immune related diseases in the liver and other organs.
evidence: Speculative inference based on multiple associations with different infections

claim: The viral load in the EAP cohort is significantly lower than that of the BOSON cohort (p=1.49×10−13).
source: For this analysis, the EAP cohort was excluded as these patients had advanced liver disease with consistently lower viral loads relative to the BOSON cohort (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by viral load comparison shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: Imputation quality was high for both rs117648444 and rs368234815 variants (information 0.974 and 0.994 respectively and certainty 0.995 and 0.997 respectively).
source: Imputation quality was high for both rs117648444 and rs368234815 variants (information 0.974 and 0.994 respectively and certainty 0.995 and 0.997 respectively).
evidence: Supported by imputation quality metrics

claim: The concordance between genotyped and imputed genotypes was 100% for both rs117648444 and rs368234815 variants.
source: The concordance between genotyped and imputed genotypes was 100% for both variants.
evidence: Supported by comparison of genotyped and imputed data
